images.caption: Figure 1:Representative WorldStream v1 runtime regions include dense city blocks, a rural settlement, streamed forest, desert terrain, and coastal terrain (top). A shared retained-state interface grounds language actions in the running world: users can ask for directions, direct nearby actors, edit present terrain, and summon distant actors (bottom).

header: 2Persistent World Representation for Streaming and Revisits

images.caption: Figure 3:WorldStream planning and realization. (a) Macro planning combines geographic evidence with cross-tile commitments. (b) A selected tile expands into a structured Micro plan encoding land use, roads, facilities, vegetation, water setbacks, and entity anchors. (c) Local generators realize that plan as connected roads, varied buildings, civic space, and a planted waterfront.

Figure 4:Terrain-and-asset realizations from persisted generated worlds. Panels show the same local-generation interface across constructed and natural settings, preserving accepted plans and geographic inputs.

Figure 6:Sequential visual cases from one continuous WorldStream runtime tour recorded at 1920×\times1080. The ordered samples show interaction and traversal through urban, rural, agricultural, forest, transition, desert, and coastal environments. Panels (a), (c), (e), (f), and (h) are crops of their source frames to make the recorded dialogue, rural dwelling, farmer and crops, forest–desert boundary, rocks, and cacti legible at three-column scale; the remaining panels show complete game-view frames.

Figure 7:Hierarchical planning ablation on the same four-Macro city-to-rural request. (a) Macro only provides settlement envelopes and a connected road skeleton but no local content. (b) Micro only uses accepted neighbors without a regional objective, retains natural land cover, and fails to form the requested settlement. (c) Flat Micro makes independent local decisions and lacks city-scale organization. (d) Without Micro-neighbor context, Macro centers and road ports remain, but tiles are repeatedly overbuilt and abrupt city/non-city cuts appear. (e) The Full hierarchy produces a connected, bounded urban-to-rural gradient.

Figure 8:Prefetch ablation over 100 route replays. (a) Four methods are compared on arrival coverage and 4 km waiting reduction; directional prefetch prepares almost the full3×33\times 3neighborhood before arrival. (b) Relative reductions obtained by adaptive lookahead over the directional policy on four lower-is-better metrics; raw directional and adaptive values are shown beside each metric.
